title: Spec: Library Assistant demo slice
description:
## Problem Statement

A school librarian who wants AI in the library today has two options: a commercial chatbot that exports student data to a vendor, or nothing. Neither lets the adults in the building see what students are asking or notice when a student discloses something a counselor needs to know. There is also no live demonstration that a librarian could install a local assistant themselves, which is what a "flox for edu" talk and a SLATE session need to show.

## Solution

A local Library Assistant that runs from one flox environment on hardware in the building (for the demo, Isaac's M5 Pro). A Teacher mints a Batch of QR Cards on their own machine and keeps the Roster there; the assistant receives only Token hashes, an expiry, and a Class label. A Student scans a Card and asks about the collection; answers are Grounded answers with Citations to Records from the school's Catalog. The Librarian watches the Live view, can Revoke a Card or Batch, and works a Flag queue fed by a deterministic Watchlist that is always on, plus optional Oversight: a second model on its own Lane that never takes capacity from the Answer lane serving Students. High-severity Flags give the Student a Supportive reply. Transcripts are Purged at the end of each school day except those attached to open Flags. Vocabulary: CONTEXT.md. Decisions: docs/adr/ 0001-0009.

## User Stories

1. As a Teacher, I want to mint a Batch of Cards for "Period 3" on my own machine, so that no server ever holds which Student has which Card.
2. As a Teacher, I want a printable sheet of QR Cards with Card numbers, so that I can hand them out at the start of class.
3. As a Teacher, I want a Roster file that stays on my machine, so that I can answer "who had card 14?" when an adult asks.
4. As a Teacher, I want to choose a Batch's expiry (e.g. one class period), so that Cards stop working when class ends.
5. As a Teacher, I want minting to work with nothing installed, so that I can use it from a locked-down school laptop.
6. As a Teacher, I want a CLI form of minting, so that I can script Batches for a whole week.
7. As a Librarian, I want to issue a registration key, so that only Teachers I trust can register Batches.
8. As a Librarian, I want Registration to accept only hashes, an expiry, and a Class label, so that I can tell a parent or DPI exactly what the assistant knows.
9. As a Student, I want to scan a Card and start asking right away, so that I do not need an account or password.
10. As a Student, I want an expired or revoked Card to tell me plainly that it no longer works, so that I know to ask the Teacher.
11. As a Student, I want to ask for books like one I loved, so that I find my next read.
12. As a Student, I want every answer to cite the Records it came from, so that I can go find the book on the shelf.
13. As a Student, I want a visible reminder that answers can be wrong, so that I learn to check the source.
14. As a Student, I want answers to stream in, so that a slow model still feels responsive.
15. As a Student who discloses self-harm or abuse, I want a caring reply that points me to a counselor, a trusted adult, and the 988 line, so that I am not shut down for speaking up.
16. As a Librarian, I want to sign in with a local staff account created on first run, so that the install works without the district's identity provider.
17. As a Librarian, I want a Live view of what Sessions are asking, labelled by Class label and Card number, so that I can see how students use it without seeing names.
18. As a Librarian, I want to Revoke one Card or a whole Batch, so that I can end misuse immediately.
19. As a Librarian, I want every Student message checked against the Watchlist for each Rubric category (self-harm, abuse, bullying, threats of violence), so that I do not have to read every transcript.
20. As a Librarian, I want the always-on Watchlist to cost no model inference, so that the whole box can serve the Students' answers.
20a. As a Librarian with a second box (e.g. two M5s), I want to point an Oversight lane at it, so that a model reviews every exchange for what the Watchlist missed.
20b. As a Librarian with one box big enough for two models, I want Oversight to run there only when no Student is waiting, so that answers never slow down.
20c. As a Librarian, I want Oversight to be off unless I configure it, and the Watchlist to keep working when the Oversight endpoint is down, so that safety never depends on a second machine being up.
21. As a Librarian, I want a Flag queue showing category, severity, the Watchlist entry that matched, Class label, and Card number, so that I can act on the worst first and see why it fired.
22. As a Librarian without a Counselor account configured, I want to work the Flag queue myself and close Flags, so that a small school can still run it.
23. As a Librarian, I want to Escalate a Flag to the Counselor, so that the right adult follows up.
24. As a Counselor, I want my own sign-in and a queue of Escalated Flags, so that I see only what was handed to me.
25. As a Counselor, I want the Flag to tell me which Teacher's Batch it came from, so that I can ask that Teacher for Identification offline.
26. As a Librarian, I want transcripts deleted at the end of each school day, so that the assistant never accumulates pupil records.
27. As a Librarian, I want transcripts attached to an open Flag kept until the Flag is closed, so that a disclosure is not lost overnight.
28. As a Librarian, I want to point the assistant at my school's Catalog through an adapter, so that it searches the collection we already maintain.
29. As a Librarian without a usable Catalog service, I want to load a MARC export into the shipped SQLite backend, so that I can still run it.
30. As a Librarian, I want the assistant to use only bibliographic fields, so that circulation and patron data can never leak into a conversation.
31. As a Librarian, I want to set the model endpoint and model names in config, so that I can use whatever OpenAI-compatible server the school runs.
32. As a presenter, I want one flox command to start the assistant and a local model server on the M5 Pro, so that the demo has no internet dependency.
33. As a presenter, I want a demo runbook (mint, scan, ask, watch, flag, revoke), so that the demo is the same every time.
34. As a presenter, I want to build a demo Catalog from Library of Congress open-access records in one setup command, then run the demo with networking off, so that no school's data is on stage and conference Wi-Fi cannot break it.

## Implementation Decisions

- One Python process (FastAPI), SQLite storage, server-rendered UI with HTMX and streaming; started as a flox service (ADR-0007, ADR-0008).
- Modules: **access** (Batch Registration, Card/Session validation, Revoke, expiry via an injectable clock), **minting** (a pure function from count, Class label, and expiry to Cards, Roster, and hashes, wrapped by an offline static page and a CLI), **catalog** (the Catalog adapter protocol plus the SQLite FTS5 backend and a MARC loader), **answer** (retrieve top-4 Records, prompt the model, stream a Grounded answer with Citations), **safety** (Watchlist matching, Flag queue, Supportive reply, Escalation), **staff** (local accounts with roles Librarian, Teacher, optional Counselor), **purge** (end-of-school-day deletion with the open-Flag exception).
- Catalog adapter interface: search(query, k) returns Records (id, title, author, subjects, summary, call number); get(id) returns one Record. No availability, no patron data (ADR-0005). Interface is expected to evolve.
- Tokens: high-entropy random secrets; the assistant stores only a hash, never the Token, never the Roster. Registration payload is exactly: list of Token hashes with Card numbers, expiry, Class label (ADR-0002).
- The model is reached through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (chat completions, and embeddings later) set in config; no cloud provider is configured (ADR-0006).
- Flagging is deterministic (ADR-0004): the Watchlist is a versioned data file of entries (pattern, Rubric category, severity), matched against each Student message after normalization (case, punctuation, common misspellings and character substitutions) and before the model is called, so a high-severity match returns the Supportive reply without spending inference.
- Lanes (ADR-0004), modelled on bead-loop's lanes: config names an Answer lane (required) and an Oversight lane (optional), each an OpenAI-compatible endpoint plus model. Oversight works a persistent backlog of exchanges. If its endpoint is on the Answer lane's host, it takes a shared lock and runs only while the Answer lane has no request in flight or queued. If its endpoint is down, the backlog is held and retried, never dropped, and is drained before the Purge. Oversight Flags record their source and time.
- The school day's end is a configured local time; the Purge runs then (ADR-0003).
- Demo hardware is the M5 Pro (24GB): a ~9B instruct model at Q4 via llama-server, whatever runs well there. Development points at llm-box's OpenAI-compatible aliases.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behaviour only: HTTP requests in, responses and stored state out. No tests of private helpers.
- The main seam is the app's HTTP API through FastAPI's TestClient. Other seams: the Catalog adapter protocol (a fake adapter), the model endpoint (a fake OpenAI-compatible server returning scripted replies), the Watchlist (a table-driven test where every entry carries messages it must and must not match), the clock (expiry and Purge), and the pure minting function.
- Every privacy ADR gets a test that would fail if it were broken: the database contains no Token or Roster data after Registration; transcripts are gone after the Purge unless Flagged; adapters never return non-bibliographic fields; no outbound call goes anywhere but the configured endpoints.
- The gate is `flox activate -- bash scripts/check.sh` (ruff + pytest); CI runs the same command.
- Prior art: the health test in the skeleton.

## Out of Scope

- Hardware detection and model recommendation (llmfit), including deciding automatically whether Oversight fits beside the Answer lane (Oversight itself is in scope, configured by hand), Elasticsearch or vendor Catalog adapters, OIDC, shelf availability, embeddings/hybrid search, a macOS installer or configurator, agent-stacks packaging, the compliance/escalation/AUP templates (Epic E), whole-school self-serve (ADR-0009), and a PII scan in the gate.

## Further Notes

- The audience is librarians and school technologists at a "flox for edu" talk and later a SLATE session; the Eau Claire middle school library is the Reference deployment afterward.
- Tickets are children of this bead. Prose for school boards stays with humans.

title: First M5 Pro baseline run (Tier A models)
description:
Tier A calibration models: Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B at int4, 4096-token prompts. Small enough to run on all three machines, which is what makes cross-machine comparison valid.

Use the mlx_transformers_benchmark methodology specifically, NOT oMLX or another harness. Published M5 Max figures for these exact models are 2,785 and 1,740 tok/s prefill, and only same-harness comparisons are meaningful. Cross-harness numbers disagree wildly: oMLX reports an M5 Pro at 466 tok/s prefill on a 27B while mlx_transformers_benchmark reports an M5 Max at 476 tok/s on a comparable 27B, which would imply zero speedup and is obviously an artifact.

Hygiene: three repetitions, report the median, plugged in, other apps closed, runtime version pinned, thermal state logged.

title: Add ollama-app cask to workstation
description:
Repo: imkarrer/workstation. File: darwin/homebrew.nix.

Add "ollama-app" to the casks list. This IS a nix-darwin-managed install because nix-homebrew is already enabled in flake.nix, so it stays declarative and in git.

Cask token is `ollama-app` (former token: `ollama`), requires macOS 14+. It symlinks /opt/homebrew/bin/ollama into /Applications/Ollama.app/Contents/Resources/ollama, so the CLI lands on PATH for free.

CRITICAL: do NOT install the Homebrew `ollama` FORMULA or nixpkgs `pkgs.ollama`. Homebrew issue #285982 documents the formula bottle shipping the MLX runner but omitting llama-server, so GGUF and embedding models fail. If the formula is present alongside the cask it wins the /opt/homebrew/bin/ollama symlink and brew only warns 'skipping link', leaving you silently on the broken binary.

Follows the repo's existing placement rule: .app bundles go in homebrew.nix as casks, like google-chrome.

title: Calibrate against published M5 Max figures
description:
Compare the b4 Tier A results against published mlx_transformers_benchmark M5 Max numbers (Qwen3.5-4B: 2,785 tok/s prefill; Qwen3.5-9B: 1,740 tok/s) to derive the EMPIRICAL scaling factor rather than trusting the theoretical one.

Expected: near 2.0x decode, 2.0-2.5x prefill. If measurement disagrees with theory, measurement wins and the plan's capacity estimates get revised.

This factor then projects every other measurement onto the Mac Studio.

title: Publish the M5 Max projection
description:
Combine c2 and c3 into one defensible projection.

From the M4 Max results: scale prefill up roughly 3.5-4x for the M5 Neural Accelerators (same 40 GPU cores, so the gain is nearly all from the new matrix hardware) and decode 1.12-1.25x for bandwidth (546 to 614 GB/s). The M5 Pro results independently confirm the M5-generation prefill multiplier is real on this specific workload.

Must answer: how many concurrent students can one Mac Studio actually serve, and does the 128GB-over-64GB argument hold up? Full residency is estimated at ~101GB (35B-A3B 23GB + gpt-oss-120b 66GB + Llama Guard 4 8GB + embeddings 2GB + Parakeet 2GB), which does not fit in 64GB.

title: Purchase decision
description:
Recommended build: Mac Studio M5 Max, 18-core CPU / 40-core GPU, 128GB unified memory, 1TB internal SSD = $5,400 (roughly $5,000-5,200 at Apple education institutional pricing).

Skip the 8TB internal SSD: it costs $3,800 and buys nothing a ~$350 external Thunderbolt 5 NVMe will not. Max the memory instead, since it is soldered and unupgradeable on a 5-7 year school asset.

CTO ladder for reference: 40-core GPU base with 48GB is $3,100; 64GB is +$400; 128GB is +$2,000; SSD 1TB +$300, 8TB +$3,800.

Timing risk: pre-orders opened Aug 25, units ship Sept 22, and the memory supply crunch is what doubled the 128GB upgrade price versus M4 Max. If board approval slips past the ship date, consider ordering early and validating after.

Gated on c4 (projection), c5 (quality), e2 (board approval).

title: Verification script: confirm MLX is actually active
description:
Repo: imkarrer/workstation.

Every failure mode in this stack is a SILENT fallback rather than an error, so this check is load-bearing for every benchmark that follows.

Assert:
  1. `which ollama` resolves into /Applications/Ollama.app/... (not a formula or nix store path)
  2. Server logs report the MLX backend, not `library=metal` or `library=cpu`
  3. The MLX dylibs are arm64 (Ollama 0.20.4 shipped x86_64-only libmlxc.dylib / libmlx.dylib that failed to load on arm64 entirely; see ollama issue #15433)
  4. macOS is 26+ so the M5-optimized mlx_metal_v4 variant is selected rather than mlx_metal_v3

Ollama 0.12.9 also shipped a regression that silently fell back GPU-to-CPU, taking users from 53 tok/s to 7. This script is the guard against shipping a benchmark run on the wrong backend.
close_reason: Verification script in ai/verify-mlx.sh; MLX v4 loaded, no CPU fallback, formula absent.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: ai/verify-mlx.sh passes: realpath into Ollama.app, mlx_metal_v4 arm64 dylibs mapped into ollama serve, macOS 26.5.1. qwen3.5:4b is Q4_K_M GGUF so the child runner is llama-server/Metal at 100% GPU; parent still has mlx_metal_v4 loaded for MLX-format models. Script warns (does not fail) on that split so benchmark rows can record the runner.

title: Quality preflight: gpt-oss-120b via hosted API
description:
No technical blockers. START EARLY, this is on the critical path to the purchase decision.

DO NOT let the librarian judge answer quality on the 24GB laptop. A 12B model will underwhelm on readers' advisory, someone concludes local AI is not good enough, and a false negative kills the project.

Instead: gpt-oss-120b is open-weight and available on hosted APIs. Run the librarian's golden question set against it via API. Those questions are about books and contain no student PII. Then run the IDENTICAL weights locally in production. Quality gets settled before a dollar is spent, without sending student data anywhere.

Depends on having the golden question set from the librarian, which is an Epic E conversation.

## What to build
The Catalog adapter seam and its first backend. The protocol: search(query, k) returns Records (id, title, author, subjects, summary, call number); get(id) returns one Record. The shipped backend loads MARC into SQLite with FTS5 and serves the protocol.

Two ways to fill it:
- **Test fixture:** a small public-domain set of Library of Congress records committed to the repo (a few hundred juvenile and young-adult titles), so a fresh checkout can search a Catalog with no network.
- **Demo Catalog builder:** a separate setup command, never run by the assistant itself, that downloads the Library of Congress MARC open-access books files (loc.gov/cds/products/marcDist.php; about 25M records from 1968 to 2014, all formats). It streams them one file at a time, keeps only juvenile and adolescent titles (the 008 target-audience byte), and loads them into SQLite. Before downloading, it checks free disk against the space it estimates it needs and stops with a clear message if there isn't enough. A partial or interrupted run can resume. It is disabled in Install config by default (ADR-0006).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Loading the fixture, then searching for a known title, returns it with all six fields
- [ ] A test proves Records carry only bibliographic fields: circulation, holds, and patron fields in the MARC input never reach a Record
- [ ] The backend is selected by config, so a second adapter is a new class plus a config value
- [ ] The builder's target-audience filter is tested on fixture records; the download itself is not run in CI
- [ ] The builder refuses to start when the disk check fails, and its README section records the measured download size, on-disk size, and record count from one real run
- [ ] `flox activate -- bash scripts/check.sh` passes

title: Compliance packet
description:
Privacy impact assessment using DPI's mini-template, data retention policy (30-45 day auto-purge with a flagged-event exception), and an AUP insert adopting DPI's AI Use Tiers (Human-Only / AI-Assist / AI-Optional) plus a student disclosure box.

Legal framing to get right:
  - Wis. Stat. 43.30 (library record confidentiality) governs PUBLIC libraries, not school libraries. Commonly conflated; get it right in the board memo.
  - FERPA and Wis. Stat. 118.125 (pupil records) are the operative rules. Chat logs tied to a student identity are plausibly pupil records, bringing parent inspection rights and a 60-day response window. Short retention plus written policy is the mitigation.
  - COPPA regulates commercial operators. A school-hosted non-commercial system is not a covered operator, which is a real structural advantage over ChatGPT or Gemini in a building full of 11-to-13-year-olds.
  - DPI's tool-vetting checklist asks whether the vendor signs a DPA, whether student data trains models, and whether data is deleted at contract end. With no vendor, all three are satisfied by construction.

REPO IS PUBLIC. Commit the template and the legal reasoning here, since a board member or another district being able to read it is a feature. The FILLED-IN assessment — real staff names, real systems, real network detail — goes in a district-controlled private location, not in git.

title: Flox agent-skills plugin (not a [skills] table)
description:
Design and prototype a first-class [skills] table for Flox manifests so project agent skills live in the environment instead of .claude/skills / .cursor/skills copies.

Why: Flox already says clone + activate is setup. That is false for the coding agent. A [skills] section is the [services] analogue for Agent Skills (SKILL.md), projected into .agents/skills on activate.

Does not violate Flox architecture if: local src= is first-class (not catalog-only), projection is generated+gitignored, harness detection uses installed dirs / the portable .agents bus rather than the current IDE process.

Proof path: convention prototype in this repo (beads skill), scanner that would feed floxify, then a product ticket under flox/product#1209 / #1240. Rust CLI / flox-manifest schema last.
design:
Proposal: package first, schema later.

Pitch to Flox is a plugin package (etc/profile.d + [plugins.flox-agent-skills]), not a [skills] table. Promote only after adoption (floxify always emits it, include-merge, discovery CLI, working-tree contract).

Repo:
- Proof: in-tree in library-ai-lab (.flox/pkgs or [hook]). No second GitHub repo.
- Share / real pkg-path: dedicated public repo + flox publish → `flox install owner/flox-agent-skills`. Lab stays first consumer.
- Flox may later take it into their catalog.

UX: plugin does not install skills.
1. Enable once: flox install owner/flox-agent-skills (or floxify).
2. Local skill: drop .flox/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; plugin auto-discovers on activate.
3. Catalog skill: flox install owner/some-skill (package drops share/skills); same projection.
4. Import: optional `flox-agent-skills import` copies .claude/.cursor skills into .flox/skills.
5. There is no `flox skills install` until a schema promotion.

Plugin scans .flox/skills/* and $FLOX_ENV/share/skills/*; [plugins] only holds targets. Dev mode only. .agents/skills gitignored.

title: AI literacy curriculum unit
description:
Runs alongside Phase 2 supervised student access.

Make RAG-grounded mode with visible citations the DEFAULT rather than an option, with persistent 'this can be wrong, check the source' framing in the UI. For a middle school this is simultaneously a safety control and the curriculum.

Be honest about the capability envelope in the teaching material: readers' advisory and catalog search are at parity with frontier models because they are retrieval-grounded; transcription actually beats cloud Whisper (Parakeet v3 at 6.32% English WER vs 7.83%); research help has a modest gap; multi-step math has a real gap and this should not be presented as a math tutor.

title: Network isolation and the library darwinConfiguration
description:
The privacy firewall, in order of how convincing each control is to a school board:

1. Default-deny outbound at the firewall. The Mac Studio's VLAN gets no egress. Model downloads and macOS updates happen in a scheduled maintenance window with a temporary allowlist. Auditable, reversible, and demonstrable in a board meeting.
2. Catalog indexed, circulation data never touched (see d1).
3. No API keys anywhere on the box, so no accidental fallback path.

Second darwinConfiguration 'library' sharing common modules with 'dev', but with the lockdown, iogpu.wired_limit_mb around 118000, and OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 rather than 30m.

Use upstream Nix, NEVER Determinate: flox does not support it. This is already the documented rule in the workstation repo.

title: MARC ingest pipeline
description:
Parse a Destiny 'Catalog > Export Titles' MARC file with pymarc, chunk and embed BIBLIOGRAPHIC RECORDS ONLY, load into the vector store.

This is the privacy firewall, expressed as architecture: the pipeline never touches patron records, checkout history, or fines. Books are indexed; who read them is not. Destiny has no bulk-MARC REST API, so this is a scheduled export plus a parse rather than a live integration, which is a feature since the boundary is enforced by the export format itself.

Document the refresh schedule and the explicit exclusion of all patron and circulation data.

title: Retrieval quality tuning
description:
Chunking strategy and retrieval tuning for readers' advisory and catalog search.

Target top-4 retrieval rather than top-8, since halving retrieved context is half of the concurrency fix.
